newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle called 0.10-0.20 ct lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle called 0.10-0.20 ct lower.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures were called down 0.10 to 0.20 cent per lb with lower beef prices and expected steady to weak cash cattle prices bearish for live cattle futures, analysts said.

"I can't see any reason to buy them (cattle futures)," said one analyst, who also noted there will be a large cattle supply this summer. "The biggest glut of cattle will be in the August time period."
Also, because of lower cash beef prices Tuesday, analysts expect meat packers will continue bidding $65.00 to $66.00 for feedlot cattle, which may be bearish for futures.
Cattle traded at $67.00 early last week, but trades slipped to $66.00 by Friday and a modest number sold at $66.00 again Tuesday in Plains area direct trade.
In addition to expected lower live cattle futures, feeder cattle may be pressured by expected higher CBOT corn futures and by ideas feeder cattle futures may be due for a correction.
"I think feeder cattle have become very toppy. I think they are due for a correction but (live) cattle will have to take them into it," said one analyst.
CBOT corn was called one to two cents per bushel higher at Wednesday's opening in reaction to forecasts for a slow developing crop in the Midwest because of cold weather there.
